newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian building firm plans $50 mln share issue.
newsitem.headline: Russian building firm plans $50 mln share issue.

text.p: Russia's OAO Manezhnaya Ploshchad plans a further $50-60 million issue of shares in November or December, after it finishes placing its current share issue in October, managing director Yuri Marinichev said on Monday.
"We expect to finish the placement this October," Marinichev told a news conference. "This money will not be enough and we are planning a (further) issue."
Manezhnaya Ploshchad, currently fully owned by the City of Mocow government, is raising funds to build a $330.50 million mall near the Kremlin.
The company plans to raise $35 million from its second share issue, which it is placing at 12,500 roubles per 10,000 roubles share.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad shares will be traded in the Russian Trading System from Tuesday or Wednesday, Oleg Yachnik, president of OLMA investment company, the lead manager of the issue, said.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad had already sold shares worth about $1 million, or about 400,000 shares, Marinichev said.
Ordinary shares will yield a dividend of 10-20 percent from 1998 to 2000 and more than 20 percent from 2000 , Marinichev said.
The project will also be financed with a credit from a German bank and pre-rental payments, he said.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad was also in talks with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development for a credit to fund one of the underground parking lots, he said.
The city government had invested half of the needed funds, said deputy mayor Iosif Ordzhonikidze.

"To think that we can find an investor for such a big project from the beginning to the end is to fool ourselves," he said. "Until the city shows that the project is economically profitable and that it's not being sparing with money for it, we cannot wait for investors."
The recuperation period for the project is between seven to eight years, with the annual profit from rent amounting to $100 million, the company said in a statement.
The price of a square meter of trading floors is $3,500 and in the restaurants and cafes will amount to $2,000, the statement said.

Manezhnaya Ploshchad trading space will amount to 25,000 square meters, restaurants and cafes will occupy 5,000 square meters and 5,000 square meters will be covered by storage houses for rent, he said.
The new mall is surrounded by other major department stores and malls -- GUM GUMM.RTS, Detsky Mir, TsUM TZUM.RTS and Petrovsky Passazh.
But Marinichev was optimistic.
Moscow has less than 0.5 square meters of trading space per capita, compared to about two square meters abroad, the company's research shows, he said.
"The huge shortage can only be solved within five to six years," he said. "We think that the mall will become Moscow's aesthetic and trade Mecca."
Manezhnaya Ploshchad is located between three metro stations, where 3.5 million people change trains every day and one of the stations will have an entrance to the mall, Marinichev said.
He said GUM rents its best trading space $4,000-$5,000 per square meter and did not have unoccupied floors.
Manezhnaya Ploshchad was in talks with 150 companies about renting trading space but have not yet concluded any agreements, Marinichev said.
--Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
